body.purpose: Sentences the operator reads: hints, explanations, empty-state copy and the legend, kept within 70-72ch.

heading-band.purpose: The account name at the head of a track band and the connection plate's page title; 15px is the largest type in the app.

heading-screen.purpose: A screen's h1, paired at the far end by a count or state readout in the quietest ink.

label.purpose: The workhorse engraving: field labels, table column headers, lamp legends, lever faces, state lines.

label-wide.purpose: Structural lettering that has to hold a wider space: INSTANCE, LEGEND, SECTION, the scope levers.

data.purpose: Anything that identifies a row - model IDs, upstream IDs, prefixes, host addresses, timestamps, the gateway's messages - in mono with tabular numerals.

data-large.purpose: The instance address on the brass instance plate and the section ID at the head of a section plate.

shadows.name: bezel-frame
shadows.purpose: The whole faceplate's edge: one neutral rule with a brass rule just inside it.

shadows.name: plate-raised
shadows.purpose: A raised plate's brass frame plus the 4% ink lip machined along its top inner edge.

shadows.name: plate-flat
shadows.purpose: A ruled plate for blocks that state rather than act.

shadows.name: lever-face
shadows.purpose: A lever's own control-rule edge and its 5% top lip; the tone's border sits just outside it.

shadows.name: lever-edge-hovered
shadows.purpose: The same inset edge turned brass under the pointer. The face is untouched, so this one rule is what a hover states.

shadows.name: well-recess
shadows.purpose: The recess of every field, route-switch channel and facts block.

shadows.name: well-focus
shadows.purpose: The brass frame a well takes while it holds focus.

shadows.name: lamp-holder
shadows.purpose: The shadow line that seats an unlit lamp in its window.

shadows.name: lamp-lit-clear
shadows.purpose: A lit green lamp: its bed plus the only outer glow in the world.

shadows.name: lamp-lit-set
shadows.purpose: A lit red lamp: its bed plus the only outer glow in the world.

motion.name: lever-response
motion.purpose: The lever face and its inset edge answering the pointer; the hover itself is an edge-colour change.

motion.name: lever-seat
motion.purpose: The key stepping 1px into the plate while held down; the face seats to the darker ground at the same moment, untransitioned.

motion.name: route-set
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: after the gateway confirms a change, a track's lamps re-light. The class is held for 700ms by the panel.

motion.name: route-set-keyframes
motion.purpose: The re-light itself: lamps come up dim and reach full inside the first 60% of the run.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce -> transition: none; animation: none
motion.purpose: Both authored motions are switched off; lamps and lever faces change instantly.

narrative.overview:
The interface is one enamelled faceplate in a dim room, and the gateway it administers is drawn on it as a diagram rather than a list. A provider is a track: a hairline-ruled band carrying the account's facts and its lamps, its models as labelled section cells along the middle, and a lever rack at its right end. Every change is a route: a two-position lever that is either set or cleared, and a ruled plate that states what the gateway answered. The diagram is never a table of rows with badges; it is an instrument an operator reads at a glance and works one handle at a time.

The world is built from material, not from decoration. There is one ground, one family of raised plates, one of sunk wells, one brass, three rules and five lamp inks — twenty declared tokens in `src/tailwind.css`, and nothing else paints. Depth is one pixel of inset rule, never a shadow, so a plate is recognisable by its brass frame and a recess by its darker ground. Lettering is *engraved*: 11px, upper case, tracked, weight 500 — cut into the metal, so it never takes a typeface's voice. Figures are *data*: the platform's mono stack with tabular digits, so IDs, prefixes and timestamps align down a column. No display face, no webfont, no image file, no icon font exists: the app ships code, the platform's own type stacks, and SVG geometry drawn on a single 16-unit grid.

Density is high and deliberately technical. State is read from lamps — 7px square windows, each with an engraved legend in the same control, so nothing is ever carried by colour alone — and every failure, refusal and confirmation is printed where the action was taken, in the gateway's own words under the panel's own headline. The panel refuses the category's resource-table-plus-badges console outright: no categorical colour chips, no avatars or illustrations, no rounded cards, no drop shadows, no hero type, no decorative icons. It also refuses to repaint silently: the one authored motion in the app is the lamps of a track re-lighting when the gateway confirms a change on it.
keyCharacteristics: One enamelled ground (`#151a1c`); depth is a 1px inset rule, never a shadow.
Square corners everywhere: radius `0` is the whole shape system.
Three brasses for structure — frames, the instance plate, rules that mean something, primary levers.
Red and green lamps carry the two aspects of every state; blue, purple and every other hue are absent.
Every lamp is drawn with its engraved legend; no state is ever colour alone.
Type is the platform's own stacks: 11px tracked upper case for labels, 13px/1.5 for prose, mono with tabular numerals for anything that identifies a row.
Bands, rules and wells instead of cards; the whole app is one faceplate closed by the same printed legend.
The gateway's message is always printed verbatim; the panel adds only what it can prove.
The single authored motion is the route-set re-light (320ms), disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

rules.name: The Two Reds Rule
rules.body: `#e0574a` lights lamps and never sets type; `#ec6a5b` sets type and never lights a lamp. A screen that needs red text uses `--color-signal`; a screen that needs a red window uses `--color-lamp-set`.

rules.name: The Control Edge Rule
rules.body: Only `--color-rule-control` may bound a control. `--color-rule` and `--color-rule-faint` divide content and may never be a lever's, a well's or a switch's own edge.

rules.name: The Lamp Legend Rule
rules.body: Every lamp is rendered inside a control or row that carries its engraved legend in the same breath — "serving", "cleared", "credential run out", "spare bay", "held". A lamp without its legend does not exist.

rules.name: The Seating Rule
rules.body: A lever's hover is carried by its edge — the shared control-rule inset turns brass and the face is left alone; its press is carried by the face — the ground seats to `#1a1f22` and the key steps down 1px, so every label gains contrast under the pointer. A hover that lightens a control's face is a regression.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Panel lettering is upper case, 11px, weight 500, 0.09em tracking — and the source text stays lower case ("read again", "save section", "lay an account with a key"); the transform shouts, not the markup.

rules.name: The Figures Rule
rules.body: Anything that identifies a row is set in `--font-data` with tabular numerals: a column of IDs, distances or counts must align digit over digit.

rules.name: The Ceiling Rule
rules.body: Type lives between 11px and 15px. If a piece of text needs to be larger than 15px to be noticed, the design is wrong, not the size.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: One account, one horizontally ruled band of the diagram — never a bordered card, never a gap between tiles. The band is 20px of vertical breathing room and one hairline, and the first band has no top rule.

rules.name: The Faceplate Rule
rules.body: Every screen ends on the same printed legend under the same faint rule. A screen does not invent a footer, a breadcrumb bar or a page title style of its own.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose stays at or under 72ch (70ch typical; 80ch only inside the legend block), and every destructive notice stays under 60ch so it is read before the lever beside it.

rules.name: The One-Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every depth cue is exactly 1px of inset rule. If a surface needs to read as raised, it gets a brass hairline; if it needs to read as recessed, it gets a darker ground and a control-rule hairline. A `box-shadow` with a blur radius is a lamp's halo or a mistake.

rules.name: The Well-Not-Plate Rule
rules.body: Raised plates never stack. A sub-block inside a raised plate is a sunk well or a flat ruled plate; the only things that may sit on a raised plate are text, rules, wells, levers and flat plates.

rules.name: The Flat-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing is emphasised until it is acted on: plates have no hover lift, no shadow change and no transition on hover. The only elements that respond to the pointer are levers (edge turns brass), wells (frame turns brass on focus), table rows (ground lifts to plate) and section cells (border turns brass).

rules.name: The Square-Corner Rule
rules.body: There is no radius token. A rounded corner of any size is a foreign material.

rules.name: The One-Grid Rule
rules.body: Every drawn mark is authored on the 16-unit grid at a 1.25 stroke with `currentColor`, so a glyph inherits the ink of whatever it sits in. No icon library, no icon font, no ``.

dos: Do take every colour from the `@theme` token set in `src/tailwind.css`. The app ships no asset file, no webfont, no image, no icon font and no third-party runtime asset — the platform's type stacks, authored SVG and these twenty tokens are the whole material.
Do draw every lamp with its engraved legend in the same control, and give the ink a tone that matches the lamp: state is never carried by colour alone.
Do use `--color-signal` (`#ec6a5b`) for red text and `--color-lamp-set` (`#e0574a`) only inside a lamp.
Do bound every control with `--color-rule-control` (`#727d84`), which clears 3:1 on the panel (4.16:1), a plate (3.86:1), a lever's raised face (3.42:1) and its seated face (3.94:1).
Do set labels in 11px engraved lettering (500 weight, 0.09em tracking, upper case, source text lower case) and every ID, prefix, URL, timestamp and count in the data face with tabular numerals.
Do keep corners square and express depth as 1px inset rules: brass frame raised, neutral frame flat, dark ground with a control-rule edge sunk.
Do put a plate's depth in its frame and its top-edge lip, and put a sub-block inside it as a well.
Do state every action's outcome where the lever is, in a message plate: the panel's headline, the gateway's message verbatim, and a fix line only where the app can prove one.
Do draw marks as authored inline SVG on the 16-unit grid at 1.25 stroke with `currentColor`; 14px for glyphs, 17–20px for the Janus mark.
Do keep motion to the route-set re-light (320ms lamps) and the 120ms lever face, and disable both under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
Do keep prose within 70–72ch, destructive notices within 60ch, and stack bands, forms and the three-column lane grid on phones instead of adding navigation chrome.
donts: Don't put a radius on anything. There is no radius token and no `rounded-*` utility in the workspace; the square corner is the shape system.
Don't add a drop shadow, a gradient, a glass or blurred surface, a coloured panel glow or a `filter`. The only outset shadow in the world is the 6px halo of a lit lamp.

Don't carry a state change on a blurred or outset shadow: hover turns a 1px inset edge brass, press seats the face to the darker ground, rows lift their ground and keys step down 1px — all by 1px and colour, all instantly.
Don't nest a raised plate inside a raised plate; use a sunk well or a flat ruled plate.
Don't introduce a display face, a webfont, an emoji or an icon library, or set type above 15px.

Don't put a raw hex value in a component or a screen where a token exists; the token set is the palette, and the only literals in the workspace are the authored SVG geometry and the themed browser surfaces.
Don't signal a state with colour alone, and don't let a lamp appear without its legend, its `aria-pressed` or its `aria-expanded` as the state requires.
Don't replace the gateway's message with a friendlier one; the gateway's words are the panel's answer.
